title: Kaushal and the Habibsters: Two Rings, Zero Trades, and a Dynasty Looking for Its Third Act
body: Every league has a founding dynasty, and the Buckaroo Football League's belongs to Kaushal. In 2023 he took the Habibsters to a 10-4 record, the No. 1 seed, and the first Buckaroo Bowl title in league history. It wasn't flawless: his worst week ever, a 74.5 dud against Sonny in Week 9, came that same season. But when the playoffs arrived, the Habibsters played like a team that already knew where the trophy was going.

Then he did it again. The 2024 Habibsters went 11-3, grabbed the top seed for a second straight year, and won Buckaroo Bowl II, making Kaushal the only manager to win the first two Bowls. He also doubled his waiver activity from 16 pickups to 32, a sign that the champ wasn't coasting. Early on, the rest of the league learned that losing to the Habibsters in December was simply part of the calendar.

2025 was the year the magic thinned out. Kaushal scored a career-high 1,973.6 points, helped by the longer 16-game schedule, and dropped his best single week ever: 151.5 points on Ramon in Week 2. Somehow all that firepower produced only an 8-8 record and the 3 seed, and the season ended at third place. The lone loss on his 4-1 career playoff record came that year, as Sonny went from back-to-back last place finishes to the Buckaroo Bowl III title.

What makes Habib's résumé so strange is how he built it: zero trades, ever, across four seasons. Everything has come through the draft and 97 total pickups, including 20 already in 2026. The head-to-head ledger says he owns Mekhi (9-2), Ramon (8-4), and Alan (7-2), and he's barely ahead of Sonny at 6-5. His only losing matchups belong to Zoe, who beat him in their lone meeting, and Randy, who leads 5-6. That makes Randy, the one manager who might trade even less than Kaushal does, his true rival in this league.

Which brings us to 2026, where the Habibsters sit at 3-4 with 797.8 points and a 15 percent shot at the title. The breaks haven't gone his way, and the waiver wire is getting a workout as a result. But this is a man who lives for college football Saturdays and knows how a season can turn in November. Count out the guy with two rings at your own risk.
